title: The Empty Will
premise: Ines Halloran, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory makes him both brilliant and haunted, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple to prove that a murder at the Vane estate has not yet happened — a prediction tied to the reading of old patriarch Edmund Vane's will. As Ines embeds himself among the heirs before the anniversary dinner, he discovers the 'closed' case of Edmund's daughter's drowning seven years ago was anything but, and that someone is orchestrating events to repeat it. The empty will — signed but leaving every line blank — turns out to be Edmund's final trap, forcing the killer to reveal themselves when the inheritance they've already spent never materializes. At the anniversary dinner, Ines exposes the murderer as the family lawyer who has been quietly rewriting lives for decades, and in doing so finds the found family he never expected among the survivors.
about_author: Oscar Brightwater is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters before turning them into fiction. He writes from a coastal town where fog is frequent and bodies are, mercifully, fictional.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Ines Halloran's POV. A pale, sweating client named Corwin pays triple his fee to prove a murder hasn't happened yet — naming a date, a house, and a victim: Lucinda Vane, drowned exactly like her mother seven years ago. Ines takes the case half out of curiosity, half unease. Beat: cold dread disguised as professional detachment.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines arrives at Vane House under cover of a routine policy audit. The estate is preparing for the anniversary dinner; portraits watch from every wall. He notices the staff flinch at the word 'dinner.' POV: Ines. Beat: creeping wrongness beneath genteel surfaces.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ines pulls the file on Eleanor Vane's drowning — ruled accidental, case closed, insurance paid. His photographic memory catches a detail everyone missed: the tide chart contradicts the timeline. POV: Ines, with flashback fragments. Beat: the closed case cracks open.

chapters.title: The Heirs Apparent
chapters.summary: Ines meets the family: brittle widow Marguerite, charming wastrel son Tobias, sharp-tongued granddaughter Wren, and the devoted housekeeper Mrs. Adeyemi. Each performs grief differently; each lies about something small. POV: Ines. Beat: suspicion distributed like place settings.

chapters.title: A Blank Where the Fortune Should Be
chapters.summary: Ines learns Edmund Vane's will exists but is sealed until the anniversary dinner — and that the lawyer, Garrick Sloane, has already hinted at its contents to different heirs in different ways. Impossible, unless the will is empty. POV: Ines. Beat: the title's mystery takes shape.

chapters.title: What Corwin Wouldn't Say
chapters.summary: Ines tracks down his client for answers and finds Corwin terrified, evasive, and clearly connected to the household — a former groundskeeper? A lover? He vanishes before Ines can pin him down. POV: Ines. Beat: the safety net frays; the investigator becomes implicated.

chapters.title: Wren's Version
chapters.summary: POV shift: Wren Vane, home after years away, watches the new 'auditor' ask questions no auditor would. She tests him, then confides she never believed her grandmother's drowning was accidental — and that Tobias was in the boathouse that night. Beat: wary alliance, first real warmth.

chapters.title: The Tide Chart Lie
chapters.summary: Ines reconstructs the night of Eleanor's death using his memory of testimony, weather logs, and the boathouse itself. Someone moved the body after death — or before. The physical evidence points to a second person on the dock. POV: Ines. Beat: methodical triumph shadowed by horror.

chapters.title: Dinner Rehearsal
chapters.summary: POV: Mrs. Adeyemi, the housekeeper, who has served three generations and kept every secret. She observes Sloane coaching the family through will-reading etiquette and notices he's rehearsed this dinner before — years ago, for Eleanor's memorial. Beat: loyalty beginning to curdle into doubt.

chapters.title: Corwin, Found
chapters.summary: Ines locates Corwin in a boarding house, half-drunk on fear. Corwin confesses he was paid anonymously to send the warning letter — and that the payment came from inside Vane House. Before he can say more, he flees. POV: Ines. Beat: the puppeteer's hand glimpsed, then withdrawn.

chapters.title: Tobias's Debts
chapters.summary: Ines digs into finances: Tobias is ruinously in debt to a lender whose paperwork traces back to Sloane's firm. Motive blooms everywhere — but too neatly. POV: Ines. Beat: power and corruption theme surfaces; money as a leash.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Memory
chapters.summary: POV: Marguerite Vane, drifting between lucidity and haze, remembers a conversation overheard the week Eleanor died — two voices in the study, one pleading, one calm. She's been dismissed as senile for seven years. Beat: the dismissed witness becomes the key.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Approaches
chapters.summary: Ines realizes the predicted murder isn't a prophecy — it's a plan, timed to the will reading when the family gathers and the house is full. He requests police help and is rebuffed: the case is closed, the family untouchable. POV: Ines. Beat: isolation; the clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Empty Frames
chapters.summary: Someone ransacks Ines's room — searching for what he knows, not what he has. His notes on the tide chart are gone, but his memory isn't. He understands now: the target of the original cover-up was never the body. It was the paper trail. POV: Ines. Beat: violation, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Sloane's Perfect Record
chapters.summary: Ines investigates Garrick Sloane: forty years as the family's lawyer, executor of every Vane death, drafter of every document. Three deaths, three wills, three fees. His memory flags a recurring signature anomaly across decades. POV: Ines. Beat: the pattern emerges like a watermark.

chapters.title: What Wren Carries
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, who reveals she received an anonymous letter too — telling her to be at the dinner or lose everything. She and Ines compare letters: same typewriter, different hands guiding it. They realize they're being cast as players in someone else's ending. Beat: found family kindling between the two outsiders.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Confession
chapters.summary: Tobias, cornered by his debts and Ines's evidence, breaks: he was there the night Eleanor died, saw a figure leave the dock, and was paid to stay silent — by Sloane, who called it 'managing the estate.' POV: mostly Ines with Tobias's raw account. Beat: guilt, relief, and a name finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Mrs. Adeyemi's Choice
chapters.summary: POV: Mrs. Adeyemi, who has known about Sloane's arrangement for years and stayed silent to protect the family she loves. She brings Ines the missing piece: Sloane's private ledger, kept in the chapel safe. Beat: betrayal of an old loyalty for a newer, truer one.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines reads the ledger: payments, forged signatures, and the draft of a will Edmund signed under duress — blank pages Sloane intended to fill after the reading. The anniversary dinner is Sloane's stage for completing a thirty-year theft. POV: Ines. Beat: full picture assembled; dread and clarity in equal measure.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: The family gathers; Sloane produces the sealed will and begins to read — and the pages are blank, just as Edmund planned, forcing Sloane to improvise. Ines watches him construct a lie in real time, matching it against the ledger in his memory. POV: Ines. Beat: coiled tension at the table; the trap springs shut.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Climax. Ines stands and recites, verbatim, the forged documents, the ledger entries, and Sloane's own words from the boathouse confession — his photographic memory turning the room into a courtroom. Sloane lunges for the fireplace and the originals; Wren and Tobias stop him. Marguerite, lucid, names the voice she heard seven years ago. Beat: catharsis; truth spoken in one breath.

chapters.title: After the Toast
chapters.summary: Resolution. Sloane is arrested; the estate passes to Wren, who offers Ines a permanent role as the family's — her family's — investigator. Corwin resurfaces, forgiven and hired. Ines, who memorized every ending but never had one of his own, raises a glass at a table where he belongs. Beat: quiet warmth; found family sealed like a signature.
